dayLines: You push through the doors into open air. Haven grounds — tents, a fire pit, worn paths. The world is that way.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 1 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 2 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
💧 A person, maybe 30s, with a wiry build returns with water: +3 clean.
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ A person, maybe 30s, with a wiry build catches you eyeing the bark plates — claw-scored, vine-laced. "...Want to actually SEE one?" They talk you through it — wide strips dried flat, laced overlapping like shingles, snug but not tight. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
💧 A person, maybe 50s returns with water: +2 clean.
💧 A man, maybe 50s, with a crooked nose returns with water: +2 clean.

"Hey." A woman, maybe 30s, with a long braid settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A woman, maybe 30s, with a long braid.)
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
Village meal: +1200 kcal, +1L water from the communal pantry. (Half ration — they don't trust you yet.)
A man, maybe 30s traded something with someone for something else. The barter economy stirs.
Nokuthula and Soo lingered over the fire together.
Nathan and Ruben lingered over the fire together.
You remember the Fire-hardened spear at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
You remember the Rain Shell at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
📓 Journal: the man in his 50s, with a shaved head taught the woman in her 30s, with a nervous tic Old World Caches.
📓 Journal: the person in their 50s taught the man in his 50s, with a crooked nose Wound Care.
— DAY 2 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.

👀 the man in his 50s, with a shaved head, the wild food forager starts a story with "back when I was a Wild food forager..." then corrects to something else mid-sentence. The correction is worse than the slip.
📓 Journal: jotted down what they said (A man, maybe 50s, with a shaved head).
A person, maybe 50s will work the garden once each day while at Haven. Other orders take priority.
You step into the Haven hall.
📋 A person, maybe 30s, with a wiry build — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
📋 A person, maybe 30s, with a buzz cut — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
(Talking costs a little energy — 10 kcal a conversation. Small talk is cheap; going deep costs time, not more food.)
Hunger gnaws. The pack is thin — work the green, haul it back, get it named at camp. That's the whole game.
"Alfredo," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Alfredo." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Alfredo).
...and then it lands: A man, maybe 30s speaks 🇮🇳 Hindi. You share no language at all.
They point at themself and say it slowly, twice. It sounds like a name: Tashi.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Tashi).
Tashi speaks only 🇮🇳 Hindi. No shared words at all — just eyes, hands, and patience.
...and then it lands: A man, maybe 50s, with a crooked nose speaks 🇺🇸 English. A few shared words. Gestures. Patience.
"Luis," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Luis." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Luis).

— Nut trees —
Hickories and oaks, heavy with mast. This is a pantry that grows.

Journal: Someone planted food here once. The trees remember.

You keep a day's food (195 kcal) — nothing extra for the pantry this time.
2 unprocessed hauls onto the counter — the clock is ticking.
Someone by the fire nods at the counter. "We pool food here. Keep what you need for the road — the rest feeds everyone, once it's food."
Nobody at the fire knows your haul any better than you do. It'll be your own hands that teach you.
You walk back into Haven. 3 Codex entries. The village is glad to see you.

Tashi has been asking about the strange leaves all week — "but what IS it?" Tonight, an answer. Alfredo is showing everyone tiny three-cornered nuts in spiny husks, under trees with smooth gray bark by the fire. "See the leaves? Like that. Don't mix it up." The journal grows — the human way.

A woman, maybe 30s, with a long braid spends the afternoon with the dusty-green diamond leaves with white mealy underside, grows in disturbed soil — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. Edible, but it argues on the way down. The fire's verdict: food, carefully. Small amounts.
From the lumped bag: Lamb's Quarters — named, and out.
★ IDENTIFIED: Lamb's Quarters. Dusty-green leaves, white powder underneath. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.

💡 You see it again in your mind: dusty-green diamond leaves with white mealy underside, grows in disturbed soil. A woman, maybe 30s, with a long braid's words land on the memory like a label. Lamb's Quarters. Of course.
A person, maybe 30s, with a buzz cut was watching. Now they know Lamb's Quarters too.
The Journal notes it: Lamb's Quarters — edible, carefully. (A woman, maybe 30s, with a long braid tested it.)
Luis: "broad paired leaves with sweet white bell flowers in spring, red berries later is coming back thick on the damp slope. Not new — but it's holding."
★ IDENTIFIED: Bael. (bel). The hard-shelled fruit — crack it like a coconut. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
Tashi brought you a sample. The Journal grows.

Fresh-cut stems on the north ground — someone else is working turf your crews use. (Ashford's foragers, most likely. You walk the ground yourself: it's thinner than your crews alone could strip it.)

Overnight, unknown shoots went bad — beyond saving. You leave it for the flies.
Fresh food keeps days, not weeks. Smoke it over a fire to make it last.

Aaron: "It offered me something. A... gift? I said no. I don't trust gifts from the sky."
